data.name: Gatiksha
data.short_meaning: Goddess of the Goals or Steps
data.long_meaning: Gati means 'goals' or 'steps'. Ksha means 'field' or 'space'. Thus, Gatiksha means 'Goddess of the Goals' or 'Goddess of the Steps'. She is believed to guide and protect those who seek to achieve their goals in life.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the journey towards personal growth and self-realization.
data.numerology_meaning: People with the life path number 8 are natural leaders and visionaries. They have strong willpower and a talent for managing resources. They are often focused on financial security and material success.

Thus, Gatiksha means 'Goddess of the Goals' or 'Goddess of the Steps'. She is believed to guide and protect those who seek to achieve their goals in life.

data.cultural_impact: The name Gatiksha holds a significant cultural influence, as it is inspired by the rich Hindu mythology and philosophy that emphasizes the pursuit of personal growth and goals. This name reflects the values of dedication, perseverance, and self-improvement, which are highly respected in Indian culture.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Gatiksha represents the divine presence of the goddess who helps individuals explore and realize their inner potential, offering guidance and support along their journey of self-discovery and personal growth. Gatiksha is symbolic of the belief that the divine is always present and active in the lives of every individual, guiding them towards their dharma or life purpose. By invoking her name, one can seek her blessings and strength in the pursuit of their goals and aspirations.

historical_references.reference: Gautami Putra Satakarni, a Satavahana king of the Andhra region, ruled from around 78 CE to 130 CE. He is also known as Mahasatakarni and Gautamiputra Bhagabhati. In later Hindu tradition, he was revered as the incarnation of the god Vishnu. The name 'Gatiksha' is derived from 'Gautami Putra', meaning 'son of Gautami'.

The Puranas mention a celestial maiden named Gatiksha, who was the mother of the goddess Parvati. In Hindu mythology, Parvati is the wife of Shiva. Gatiksha is also referred to as the 'Mother of Parvati'.
